description:
## Why this ticket exists

MCP is leg (2) of the product vision: a user's Claude answers "what did I spend this week per project". The v0.2 shape was set by Codex review: round 2 CUT `usage_hourly` (compute-on-demand could invoke the 60–80 s pipeline inside a 60 s client timeout), forced the cursor contract and the query-tz-equals-snapshot-tz rule, and split the reader computation lease into its own namespace; round 3 demoted the SDK choice from an assumption to the T-009 release gate (v1 `registerTool` takes a zod raw shape, v2 a full `z.object` — NOT drop-in). Since then two gates this ticket depends on have reported: T-008 decided the coordination primitive (kernel-held loopback port bind; both lockfile candidates disproven — `docs/v0.2-prototype-findings.md`), and the SDK verdict plus its consumption rules are recorded as delegated decisions in N-003. Both are folded below.

## Scope — in

- **`spendbar mcp`** on the same bin; stdio transport; **stdout carries JSON-RPC only**, all logs to stderr (stdout purity is a T-009 conformance test).
- Tool layer sits behind the **~50-line adapter produced and validated by T-009** — never against an SDK directly. **SDK decided (T-009 verdict, N-003 delegated decision): adopt v2.** `@modelcontextprotocol/server@2.0.0` enters the ROOT manifest as a regular dependency pinned EXACT (no `^`/`~`) only when the production adapter lands in `src/mcp` (this ticket's consumption) — never while candidates live in the isolated spikes workspace; `zod` enters as an exact-pinned DIRECT dependency (T-009's phantom-dependency finding). Version bumps are deliberate acts gated by re-running T-009's conformance suite and supply-chain inspection, the same pattern as ccusage bumps.
- **Exactly 5 tools**: `usage_summary`, `usage_by_project`, `usage_by_day`, `usage_share`, `usage_blocks`. **`usage_hourly` is NOT registered** until a bounded snapshot-backed implementation exists (later it is constrained to cached ranges with a typed unavailable/stale response and an internal deadline below the client timeout). Do not register a stub.
- **Strict input schemas**: normalized start/end dates, provider filters, sort, limit, cursor; malformed input yields typed validation errors, never crashes (cautionary precedent: ISS-017 — the Python CLI tracebacks on `hourly --date <non-ISO>`; MCP must validate).
- **v0.2 timezone rule**: the query timezone must equal the snapshot's IANA timezone (from T-010's per-generation tz + day-boundary policy) — validation error otherwise; timestamp-level re-bucketing is explicitly future work.
- **Cursor contract**: a cursor encodes dataset generation id + normalized query + sort key + position; the referenced immutable generation is retained for a bounded period (implemented against T-010's retention/GC); expired cursors return a typed error requiring pagination restart; mismatched query/sort in a presented cursor is rejected typed. Hard range/row caps; truncation + `nextCursor` metadata; summary-first defaults.
- **`outputSchema` registered once in `tools/list`**; every result = `structuredContent` + concise text fallback; `generatedAt`/freshness/coverage/warnings live INSIDE the registered result schema, derived per requested range/fields from T-010's per-dataset provenance — no global stale flag.
- **Reader ephemeral computation lease — an OPTIMIZATION, not a correctness boundary** (per T-008's verdict, findings §3.3/§3.5): store correctness comes from T-010's atomic-rename publish — a reader never sees a torn snapshot, lease or no lease — so the lease exists solely to avoid duplicate expensive recomputation when the snapshot is stale and no service is live. It is a namespace of the ADOPTED T-008 primitive: its own write-once `link()` port allocation and its own required `purpose` string, distinct from the writer singleton's (domain separation is what stops a reader lease answering the writer's HMAC challenge, or vice versa). There are **no ownership records, no expiry rules, and no takeover protocol** — the primitive has nothing to reclaim: exclusion holds exactly while the holder's listener stays bound, holder death releases the port at the kernel, and a contender then simply rebinds the persisted port. A live-but-unresponsive holder is never taken over (timeout-based reallocation recreates the split-owner race T-008 eliminated); waiting readers run to a bounded deadline and return existing data with honest freshness. The holder computes a bounded in-memory top-up in a **private temporary generation that never touches promoted writer shadows**; subprocess concurrency capped; **multi-client herd load test** (a v0.2 phase exit criterion). Because the lease is advisory, its residual overlap window (findings §3.5: the kernel frees the port before the old holder's JS observes the close) costs duplicate work at worst — never corruption, and the private-generation rule keeps even that out of the writer namespace.
- **CLI gains `--cached`**: answer from the snapshot only, never invoking ccusage. `--cached` alters CLI surface the frozen oracle governs, so every user-visible divergence it introduces ships through the established parity mechanism — a numbered ALLOWLIST divergence entry plus replacement shipped-mode tests (ISS-026 pattern D); byte parity is untouched wherever the flag is absent.
- **CI measures tool-definition token cost — budget rule decided (N-003, resolving former open question 4):** at this ticket's completion, record the measured `tools/list` serialized size and proxy-token count for the 5 real tools as the committed baseline, and hard-gate CI at **baseline +10%**. Regressions past the ceiling are breaking changes. (T-009 ships the decision-neutral measurement plumbing; the enforced budget lands here.)

## Scope — out

- `usage_hourly`; timezone re-bucketing; MCP resources/prompts (tools only); any non-stdio transport.
- Registration UX: `claude mcp add`/`codex mcp add` consent prompts belong to the v0.3 setup wizard; `doctor`'s MCP-registration health checks and the real-client launch matrix are v0.3. (Note for the exit test: the plan routes MCP registration through the launcher — shebang bins break under GUI-launched clients without the package manager's PATH.)

## Failure modes to test

- **No/crashed service**: reader-lease path serves; lease holder killed mid-computation → the kernel releases the lease port and a successor contender may rebind and compute, or every reader returns honest-stale at the bounded deadline — no deadlock, and no stale-state takeover step exists to exercise (death releases the port; nothing is reclaimed). The private temp generation is never promoted and never visible to other readers as authoritative (assert the writer namespace is untouched).
- **Herd**: many simultaneous MCP clients + `--cached` CLI against a stale snapshot → exactly one computation while the holder's listener stays bound, subprocess count ≤ cap, every caller answered (fresh or honest-stale) within the bounded deadline.
- **Domain separation**: a challenge using the writer's `purpose` against the lease port (and the converse) is refused — a reader lease must not be able to impersonate the writer singleton.
- **Concurrent refresh**: the writer publishes a new generation mid-pagination → the cursor stays pinned to its generation and pages remain mutually consistent until retention expires, then typed expiry.
- **Corrupt data**: quarantined generation ⇒ bounded partials from the known-good generation with warnings — no fabricated totals.
- **Protocol**: T-009's conformance suite (initialize, tools/list, tools/call, malformed input, cancellation, EOF, stdout purity) rerun over the final tool layer against recorded real-client transcripts.

## Dependencies on gate outcomes

- **T-009 (hard — verdict recorded)**: SDK decision + adapter + real-client transcripts; this ticket's tool layer is written against that adapter, on the adopted v2 SDK. T-009's amended go/no-go defines `blocked` (neither SDK passes) as a valid COMPLETED outcome — on `blocked`, T-009 creates a resolution ticket and adds it to THIS ticket's blocked-by, precisely because bare completion would otherwise satisfy `T-013.blockedBy`. So the start condition here is the recorded verdict (adopt v2), not T-009's completion status alone; if the verdict ever changes, look for a resolution ticket in blocked-by before proceeding.
- **T-010 (hard)**: all reads come from generation snapshots; freshness/coverage/warnings map from per-dataset provenance; cursor retention rides generation retention/GC; quarantine ⇒ bounded partials. T-010's atomic publish is also what makes the lease advisory (see Scope).
- **T-008 (COMPLETE — verdict consumed)**: the gate rejected both lockfile candidates (a lock file must be reclaimed after owner death, and Node has no atomic compare-and-delete or flock) and adopted the kernel-held loopback port bind with write-once `link()` allocation. The computation lease is a namespace of THAT primitive — own allocation, own `purpose` — and inherits its honest contract: exclusion exactly while the listener stays bound.
- **T-011 interplay (deliberately NOT a blocker)**: MCP must work with NO live service — that is what the lease exists for — but the "warm" exit criterion presumes a warm snapshot; tests must cover both the live-service and no-service worlds.

## Constraints

No lifecycle scripts or native builds; `package.json` never carries an author field; no real transcript data or personal paths in fixtures (MCP fixtures synthetic); `usage.py` stays frozen — MCP semantics derive from the ported TS core; D5 byte-parity governs CLI text output (with `--cached` divergences riding the numbered ALLOWLIST, above), while MCP structured outputs are separately versioned public schemas derived through adapters from the independently versioned internal snapshot schema (round-2 decoupling: NOT "internal schema written from MCP schemas").

## Exit

Week-per-project < 2 s warm from BOTH real clients (Claude Code and Codex).

## Acceptance criteria
1. `tools/list` returns exactly the 5 named tools, each with `outputSchema` registered once; a test asserts `usage_hourly` is absent.
2. Conformance suite green over the adopted v2 SDK behind T-009's adapter, against recorded real-client transcripts: initialize, tools/list, tools/call, malformed input (typed errors, no crash), cancellation, EOF; zero non-JSON-RPC bytes appear on stdout in any test.
3. Timezone rule: a query whose timezone differs from the snapshot's IANA timezone returns a validation error naming both zones; an equal-timezone query succeeds.
4. Cursor contract: paging past the row cap yields truncation + nextCursor; all pages of one cursor are consistent with a single generation even when the writer publishes mid-pagination; after the referenced generation ages out of bounded retention, the cursor returns the typed expired error; a cursor whose embedded normalized query or sort key mismatches the request is rejected with a typed error.
5. Freshness honesty: with a stale snapshot and no service, results carry freshness/coverage/warnings reflecting actual per-range coverage; with a quarantined generation, results are bounded partials from the known-good generation with warnings — never fabricated totals.
6. Reader lease herd test (v0.2 exit): N ≥ 10 concurrent clients against a stale snapshot produce exactly one computation while the holder's listener stays bound, subprocess count never exceeds the cap, and every client receives fresh or honest-stale data within the bounded deadline. Killing the lease holder mid-computation ends in either a successor computation (kernel-released port rebound by a contender) or honest-stale at the deadline — never deadlock, and never any expiry/takeover step. The promoted writer namespace is bit-identical before/after (private temp generations never promoted), and a writer-`purpose` challenge against the lease port is refused (domain separation).
7. `spendbar <view> --cached` spawns no ccusage subprocess (asserted via the injected runner) and returns snapshot-derived output with a freshness indication.
8. Parity: every user-visible divergence introduced by `--cached` has a numbered ALLOWLIST entry plus replacement shipped-mode tests, and the byte-parity suite stays green for all non-`--cached` invocations.
9. v0.2 phase exit: a week-per-project query completes in under 2 s warm from BOTH real clients (recorded wall-clock with repetitions; deterministic proxies — sizes, query counts — hard-gate in CI).
10. Token budget (N-003): CI records the `tools/list` serialized size and proxy-token count; at ticket completion these are committed as the baseline, and CI fails hard when either exceeds baseline +10%.

## Risks
SDK v2 immaturity was the plan's #5 top risk; v2 is now adopted through T-009's gate, so any late SDK surprise lands on this ticket — the adapter plus the v1 backend T-009 built remain the contained fallback. Cursor-generation retention couples reader lifetimes to writer GC: a bug either leaks generations (disk growth) or breaks pagination mid-flight with untyped failures. The lease's liveness hazards are narrower than first framed but real: orphaned-lease deadlock is designed out (the kernel frees the port on death), but a live-hung holder pins every reader to the wait deadline, and a bad deadline value turns each stale read into a stall — the herd and kill-the-holder tests are mandatory, not nice-to-have. The token-cost gate protects every user's context window at every client session start; the +10% ceiling makes regressions breaking changes by rule.

## Open questions (owner decisions)
1. Bounded retention period for cursor-referenced generations (the plan mandates 'bounded' but gives no number; it also sets T-010's GC floor of at least one known-good generation).
2. Reader-lease wait deadline and subprocess concurrency cap values (unspecified).
3. Scope of `--cached`: all 9 ported CLI views or only the snapshot-expressible subset? And its behavior when NO snapshot exists at all (typed error vs empty output).
4. Whether the v0.2 real-client exit test registers the server via the launcher's explicit `mcp` mode or via validated absolute paths (the launcher-registration requirement is stated in the plan; the doctor/upgrade matrix that exercises it is v0.3).
5. usage_blocks payload contract, restated with current facts (ISS-026 pattern C): ccusage `blocks --json` DOES have pinned bundled-schema contract coverage (added under ISS-002); the residual gap is that no RUNTIME validator covers custom `CCUSAGE_CMD` payloads, which ISS-023 records as an accepted parity tradeoff for the CLI. Does that acceptance extend to MCP structured outputs, or must `usage_blocks` gain a runtime validator (inside this ticket or as a prerequisite fix) before serving `CCUSAGE_CMD`-shaped payloads?

**Related issues:** ISS-002, ISS-004, ISS-017, ISS-023, ISS-026, ISS-030, ISS-033

park.reason:
PARKING T-013 at plan round 1. Three of its ten acceptance criteria cannot be discharged, and every resolution is either an owner decision or requires the parked T-011. Re-planning would not change that set, so another round would only polish a plan for work that cannot be built.

BLOCKER 1 — AC 4 (cursor contract) has no API to be built on. The contract requires all pages of one cursor to come from a single pinned generation even when a writer publishes mid-pagination. T-010 exposes no reader that loads a requested generation id: readSnapshot always follows the CURRENT manifest (src/snapshot/store.ts:2581), so a pinned id cannot be retrieved and page 2 silently walks the NEW active generation — the wrong-answer-wearing-a-correct-shape failure the criterion exists to prevent. Implementing it needs a new hardened T-010 readGeneration(fs, paths, generationId) carrying the same containment, exact-mode, decoding and race checks as readSnapshot. That is new T-010 surface, not T-013 work. Retention has the same shape: createPin requires a LatchingWriteAuthority and writes through the writer's staging/pins namespace (store.ts:3068), which a reader lease in its own purpose namespace cannot hold and must not impersonate — and with T-011 parked no GC runs, so pins would accumulate unbounded.

BLOCKER 2 — AC 6 (reader lease) cannot be satisfied, and the lease is not implementable as the ticket specifies it. Filed as ISS-079 (critical). Four ticket properties cannot coexist: the holder computes a top-up; every caller is answered within a bounded deadline; the result is NEVER promoted; and the measured pipeline is 60-80 s with no --since speedup. Any deadline fails — large enough to cover the work and it is not a client-facing bound (MCP clients time out near 60 s, the reason round 2 cut usage_hourly); small and a waiting holder violates it, a cancelling holder never completes a COLD computation, and a detaching holder is a short-lived MCP or CLI process that exits on stdio EOF and kills the only computation. Never-promoted means finished work benefits nobody. The herd test HIDES this rather than catching it: N clients, exactly one computation, everyone answered — all satisfied by killing that computation and serving stale, so the test passes while the feature does nothing. The three coherent fixes are all owner decisions and two route through T-011: let the holder wait the pipeline bound (needs a durable result, contradicting never-promoted), own background computation in a persistent service (T-011), or promote an atomic cache under shared writer authority (T-011's authority, and it makes the lease a correctness boundary rather than the optimization the ticket calls it). AC 6 additionally requires a live-service world that cannot exist while T-011 is parked — and the reviewer was right that labelling that deferral honestly does not close it.

BLOCKER 3 — the lease would require building all of T-011's unbuilt coordination stack. src/service and src/mcp do not exist and spikes/locking is explicitly evidence rather than a library, so lease.ts has no fs or net adapter, no runtime-directory or token ownership, no write-once publication and no coordination artifact inventory — leaving exact 0700/0600 modes, coordination fsync, short-write handling, post-link irreversibility and the native-error boundary all unestablished. And the lease's private computed generation must carry Provenance including ccusageFetchedAt, so the compute path inherits ISS-075 after all: my reader-only exemption covered READING a snapshot, not COMPUTING one. That was my error and it is recorded as such.

ONE CONFLICT THE OWNER SHOULD SEE, separate from the blockers. My Q5 decision — requiring a runtime validator for usage_blocks under CCUSAGE_CMD — silently reversed a recorded decision: ISS-023 accepted that gap and ISS-026 explicitly extends the acceptance to T-013. My reasoning may justify reopening it (an LLM computing over unvalidated payloads and presenting results as fact is a different blast radius from one terminal), but reasoning does not authorize overriding a decision already made. T-013 must align with ISS-023/ISS-026 or carry a new recorded decision superseding them for MCP.

WHY ROUND 1 RATHER THAN ROUND 7. T-011 took seven rounds and 80 findings before I accepted that its blockers were structural, and I declined park four times on the way. The same evidence here arrived in one round: two criticals, both structural, plus three feasibility findings that route through missing APIs and a parked ticket. About ten of the fifteen findings are things I can fix — the payload schema, the nine-view --cached table, the config bounds, the zod pin, the AC 1 duplicate-registration test, the section 1/section 7 contradiction — and fixing them would leave every blocker untouched. Recognising that in round 1 is the lesson from T-011 applied rather than restated.

WHAT SURVIVES. The plan is preserved at docs/t013-mcp-server-plan.md, alongside docs/t011-headless-service-plan.md. The reader-side design that is NOT blocked is sound and reviewed: the five bounded tools, strict input schemas, the timezone rule against Provenance.timezone, freshness derived per range and per field from coverage/fieldCoverage with absence reported as not-covered, bounded partials from quarantined generations, stdout purity, and the token budget. A re-scoped T-013 covering ACs 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8 and 10 — the pure reader surface — looks buildable today, but selecting that subset is a re-scope and therefore the owner's call, not mine to make by planning around the criteria I cannot meet.

T-013 should return to open and be reworked once ISS-079 is decided, ISS-075 is resolved, T-010 gains a generation-scoped reader, and T-011 is unparked.

title: MCP server: 5 bounded tools + reader computation lease + --cached
